Section 1 starts below a casing shoe at 2561.8 m MD and sets no casing.
Section 2 starts below a casing shoe at 2561.8 m MD and sets casing with its shoe at 2914.8 m MD.

Section 13 starts below a casing shoe at 3231.0 m MD and sets no casing.
Section 14 starts below a casing shoe at 2914.8 m MD and sets no casing.
Section 15 starts below a casing shoe at 1368.4 m MD and sets no casing.
Primary lost time totals 421.25 h, 23.14 % of the wellbore activity time.
By cause, primary lost time is 383.0 h of waiting on weather (interruption -- waiting on weather), 34.5 h of repair (interruption -- repair) and 3.75 h of fishing (interruption -- fish).
By section, section 2 has 135.25 h of primary lost time, 56.35 % of its activity time.
Section 9 has 4.75 h, 9.9 % of its activity time.
Section 12 has 5.5 h, 4.17 % of its activity time.
Section 13 has 1.25 h, 1.04 % of its activity time.
Section 14 has 262.0 h, 47.38 % of its activity time, the largest block of primary lost time on the wellbore.
Section 15 has 12.5 h, 32.89 % of its activity time, all coded repair.
Sections 1, 3, 5 and 7 have no primary lost time, and sections 4, 6, 8, 10 and 11 have no lost-time rows at all.

Possible lost time, kept separate and not added to the primary figures, totals 75.75 h, 4.16 % of the wellbore activity time, coded mostly as interruption -- other (63.0 h), interruption -- maintain (11.75 h) and drilling -- wait (1.0 h); these codes may or may not be lost time.
By section, the largest possible lost time is 24.25 h in section 3, which is 52.43 % of that section's activity time, and 21.25 h in section 1, which is 12.57 % of its activity time.
On 2009-01-19 the rotary steerable tool could not hold toolface in the 12.25 in section and the decision was recorded to pull out and change it.
On 2009-01-24 a casing joint was driven off the pipe-handling rollers and operations were stopped for a time-out and investigation, coded as possible lost time of 5.0 h.
From 2009-01-29 to 2009-02-04 the rig waited on weather to run the production riser, 132.5 h in total over 13 activities coded primary, in section 2.

On 2009-02-25 the tubing-hanger running tool showed communication between the two safety-valve control chambers, and repairing it (seal change and back-up tool preparation) took 3.75 h of primary lost time in section 9.
On 2013-10-10 a slickline toolstring parted below the cable head, leaving a fish in the hole.
Fishing for the parted toolstring and the left-in-hole tool took 3.75 h of primary lost time (interruption -- fish).
On 2013-10-18 repeated attempts to release the tieback adjustable-sub running tool failed, 2.75 h of primary lost time.

From 2013-10-18 the rig waited on weather to pull the production riser, and from 2013-10-30 it waited on weather again before running the riser; waiting on weather accounts for most of the 262.0 h of primary lost time in section 14.
On 2013-11-07 the seal assembly hung up on the shear seal at the wellhead; this led to wellhead jetting, a mill run and repeated seal-assembly runs through 2013-11-09, coded as repair.

Weather waiting dominated primary lost time, both while running the production riser in the first campaign and while pulling and re-running it in the plug and abandonment campaign, so the next well should schedule riser and BOP operations for a weather window and agree a weather limit with a pre-planned maintenance list, rather than relying on maintenance filling the wait.

The plug and abandonment campaign spent a large share of its section 14 time waiting; the next P&A should sequence riser pulling early and have the casing crew and helicopter logistics confirmed before the weather-sensitive step, since one wait was also tied to a cancelled crew flight.

The failures of the slickline toolstring (parted and fished) and of tieback and seal-assembly running tools show that wellhead and tool-release hardware should be function-tested at surface before running, and that fishing tools should be on deck when wireline jarring is planned.

Rig-floor equipment faults (pipe-handling rollers, elevators, top drive hydraulics and the pipe-racking systems) generated possible lost time in sections 1, 3 and 7; the next well should check and spare this equipment before casing and completion running starts.

The daily reports leave hole size unknown for most sections and show a section start depth that is deeper than its end depth, so the next well's reports should record hole size and section depths consistently to allow correct section-level rate and casing review.

row.comments: Reciprocated on stand whilst discussing situation with town. Decided to POOH to change Powerdrive.

Held time out for safety and troubleshoting after a 9 5/8" casing joint was driven off of the HTS power rollers. Made up and ran 9 5/8" casing joint on HTS, installed swadge and kelly cock. Investigated incident. The 9 5/8" was tilted resting on the roller frame and the deck. The area in which the casing joint tilted was barriered off according to standard procedure for running HTS/PDM. Revised practice for picking up casing until further notice, i.e. only one joint on HTS rollers and HTS at the time.
Made up 9 5/8" x 10 3/4 x-over. RIH with 10 3/4" 60,7# 13Cr80 VamTop casing from 1113 m to 1580 m MD. Filled every 10th casing joint with OBM.

Waited on weather to run production riser.

Meanwhile :
-Brought thension cylinders to Centralizer deck
-Replaced tension cylinders
-Changed wire on drillfoor yellow and black tugger
-Trobleshot HTS - no clear fault indication - random behaviour at w.r.t. stop point
-Performed maintenance of drawwork
-Emptied pit #5 into skips

Waited on weather to run production riser.

Meanwhile :
-Emptied pit#5 into skips
-Perfromed NDT on drilling equipment
-Changed oil on TDS
-Greased C/K manifold
-Tidied wellhead module
-ROV brushed, cleaned and inspceted F-15 wellhead

Waited on weather to run production riser. Wind checks performed on rig floor, cantiliver and derrick.

Meanwhile :
-Cleared centralizer deck and brought thension cylinders down. 
-Cleared rig floor to access TDS.
-Inspected gasket on BOP stump and landed BOP. 
-MU NT2 connector on BOP stump. Opened BOP for 3 montly PM.
-Mixed and injected slop in F-14.
-Trouble shot on pipe handler (HTS) alignement.
-Performed NDT on drilling equipment.
-Brought tension cylinders up.

Waited on weather to run production riser.

Meanwhile :
-Performed NDT on drilling equipment.
-Re-landed and MU NT2 connector on BOP stump. Prepared for pressure testing BOP.
-Finished trouble shooting on pipe handler (HTS) alignement.
-Removed tension sylinders from rig floor.
-Removed riser spider and installed master bushings to access iron roughneck.
-Started to disassemble aft iron roughneck.
-Performed maintenace on kill and standpipe manifolds.

Waited on weather to run production riser.

Meanwhile :
-Instructed used of deluge/foam system on wellhead to crew as a part off weekly drill.
-Pressure tested BOP on stump. Ok.
-Disassembled and moved aft iron roughneck.
-Disconnected fwd iron roughneck and moved to aft position.
-Installed iron roughneck in aft position.
-Installed two-part nylon protector guides and tension ring on F-15.
-Vibration tested slurry pump.

Waited on weather to run production riser.

Meanwhile :
-Function tested iron roughneck in aft position.
-Cleaned lower shakers.
-RU to run tuggers through F-10 opening on centralizer deck.
-Worked on motor for slurry pump.
-Removed master bushings. Installed and function tested riser spider.
-Built scaffolding/barriers around deck openings.

Waited on weather to run production riser. Informed Production to re-start wells at 15:05.

Meanwhile :
-Performed rig maintenace
-Performed derrick inspection/PM's in derrick.
-Assembled slurry pump.
-Cleaned lower shakers
-Performed 3-yearly maintenace on valve C3
-Finished function test of iron roughneck

Waited on weather to run production riser. Informed Production to shut down F-4, F-5 and F-14 at 08:10.

Meanwhile :
-Performed rig maintenace
-Routed tuggers to guide TBC/production riser.

Waited on weather to run production riser. 

Meanwhile :
-Performed rig maintenace
-Performed NDT on drilling equipment
-Performed 3-yearly maintenace on valve C3
-Cleaned lower shakers
-Installed rollers on PRS lower arm

Waited on weather to run production riser.

Meanwhile :
-Performed 5-yearly maintenance on choke manifold (C13 and C16)
-Performed maintenance on slips.
-Performed maintenace on drag chain on main deck.
-Cleaned lower shakers
-Changed rollers on aft PRS
-Trouble shot E-stop on fwd iron roughneck

Waited on weather to run production riser. 

Meanwhile :
-Performed 5-yearly maintenance on choke manifold (C13 and C16)
-Cleaned lower shakers
-Installed flush joint on aft PRS
-Performed NDT on drilling equipment
-Emptied water from below BOP NT2 connector

Waited on weather to run production riser. 

Meanwhile :
-Performed 5-yearly maintenance on choke manifold; C16
-Cleaned lower shakers
-Re-arranged the half-moon hatches in moonpool to avoid hanging up when RIH with PR
-Cleaned and backloaded lifting eyes for BOP
-Replaced hang-off supporters for flowline on XMT deck
-Cleared rig floor off flush joint elevators, cherry picker, slings etc
-Performed NDT on drilling equipment
-Errected scaffolding around moonpool hatches

Waited on weather to run production riser. Informed Production to shut down F-4, F-5 and F-14 at 01:35 hrs.

Meanwhile :
-Performed 5-yearly maintenance on standpipe manifold; C8
-Cleaned lower shakers
-Recovered moonpool 10 MT tugger from seabed
-Held tool box meeting for untangeling guide wires and running PR
Investigated problem. Found indication of communication between the ASV and DHSV chambers in the communication collar and running tool.
Disconnected control lines from running tool. Laid out primary running tool. Changed out seals on communication collar. Prepared back up running tool.
POOH from 284 m to surface. Toolstring parted at time delayed release below cable head.
Attempted to release adjustable sub tool several times. No success.
Pressured up string to 140 bar to work tool pistons. M/U tieback string w/ 5 right hand turns. Attempted to release DQ tool w/o success.
Attempted to release DQ tool on surface w/o success.

Waited on weather to pull production riser.

Meanwhile performed general rig maintenance:
Assisted hydraulic mechanic on derrick work basket
Removed equipment from moonpool.
Maintenance and preparation for changing wires on fwd and aft PRS.

Held Statoil TOFS with deck crew #3 and third party personnel.

Waited on weather.

Meanwhile:
Cleaned and tidied wellhead deck and drill floor.
Performed planned maintenance.
Cleaned BOP's prior to pressure test.
Installed BOP test mandrel.

Picked up seal assembly RT with "used" seal assembly (White painted).
RIH with seal assembly to below BOP.
POOH with seal assembly and inspected same, no damage observed.
RIH with seal assembly to 137 meter, hang up on shear seal, sat down 12 Ton.

Picked up and RIH with wearbushing RT and jetsub assembly.
Jet washed WH with 3050 liter/min, 55 bar.
Engaged wearbushing and pulled free with 20 ton overpull.
Confirmed measurement to WH.
POOH with wearbushing and jetsub assembly, laid down same.
